readmodels.title: Seat Availability
comments: Time slots have no origin in the model. Seat Availability.timeSlot and .reservationDate are mapped to Reservation Made.*, but the slot grid (18:00 / 20:00 / 22:00) exists before anyone books - a slot with zero reservations must still show a row, and today nothing on the board creates one. Is the slot list fixed configuration (then say so in a note and change the mapping to derived:), or is there a missing concept that belongs next to 'seats' in Managing Tables?

commands.title: Make Reservation
comments: No clock is modelled. The scenario 'Cannot book a date in the past' states the current date in prose only (description: 'The current date is 10.09.2026'). Same limitation as 'Can only cancel if not started yet' in Vacation Planning. A human reads it fine; a code generator cannot. Should current-date be an explicit command input, or is prose accepted here?

screens.title: Book a Table
comments: The blank-creation-form exemption claimed for this screen in Step 5i does not hold as rendered. This copy has no incoming READMODEL and was exempted as a form with no prior state - but its marked component contains a time-slot <select> listing 18:00 / 20:00. Those options ARE prior state, and Make Reservation.timeSlot is mapped 'user-input' with nothing on the board supplying the choices. Resolve one of two ways: (a) connect Seat Availability -> this screen and drop the exemption, or (b) declare the slot list fixed configuration and say so in a note. Same root cause as the time-slot QUESTION on Seat Availability.

commands.title: Cancel Reservation
comments: reservationId is mapped 'user-input', but the issuing screen (My Reservation) IS connected to the My Reservation read model and displays this value - so the field does have a board source, unlike Make Reservation's inputs. Should the mapping be 'My Reservation.reservationId' to reflect that the guest selects a displayed reservation rather than typing an id? The accepted no-guest-identity decision (see the Notes lane in this column) explains why there is no session lookup, but it does not require the mapping to be user-input.
